name: off_by_one_comparison
description: Forward-scanning implementation that uses <= instead of < when deciding whether the current numeral is smaller than its neighbor, so two adjacent numerals of EQUAL value are wrongly treated as a subtractive pair and cancel out instead of adding (III -> -1, LVIII -> 54). A very plausible off-by-one when writing the lookahead comparison. Standard non-repeating subtractive forms like IV/IX still come out correct, so this control is only caught by the repeated-numeral hidden tests.
